title: The Shulammite
lead: The Shulammite (hashulammit) is the woman called back in Song of Songs 6:13. The name is most likely 'the woman from Shunem', though it may be the feminine of Solomon's name or a pet name from shalom. Some readers have made her the heroine of the whole Song, with Abishag of Shunem as her historical model, but that is a view, not a fact.

sections.b: Shunem was a town in Issachar in the Jezreel valley (Joshua 19:18; 1 Samuel 28:4). Abishag the Shunammite was brought to King David in his old age to warm him (1 Kings 1:1–4), and a woman of Shunem housed Elisha (2 Kings 4:8–37). The Greek of Song 6:13 has Soumaneitis, 'Shunammite', and the Latin has Sulamitis. The change of the letter n to l between Shunammite and Shulammite is known in other Semitic languages.
